P1.evidence: Setter notes existed and were referenced but not read back - 'I got some of the notes from Kyla yesterday, but I mean, curious, like how can we potentially help?' - so the prospect got no sense of being pre-understood. The frame ran the usual two of four parts: 'understand where you're at with your fitness right now. What it is you're looking to accomplish.' Frame agreement was taken and given. The open question used the coached phrasing again, which is the second call in a row showing that uptake.

P2.evidence: Age (30), weight (155 lb) and body fat (a little over 15%) were all volunteered and none were asked; height was stated but is garbled in the transcript. The largest omission is occupation - on a 44-minute call with a prospect who travels for weeks at a time for conferences and describes an intensive work schedule, the rep never asked what he does for a living, which also leaves the ICP untestable. Health conditions were never asked. The SI joint injury was volunteered and then followed up reasonably - 'where are you noticing that in your workouts or just in your day-to-day?' - which produced the posture and lifting triggers, but there was no question about duration, treatment or restriction. Training was covered thoroughly, including the crucial two-weeks-on, three-weeks-travelling pattern. Nutrition is a genuine hit and among the best in the batch: meal plans, macro history, protein targets, home versus eating out, Uber Eats, and alcohol were all asked. Sleep and energy were never asked and appear only as things the programme would later track.

P3.evidence: The surface layer was handled well - target physique, mobility and flexibility, and a concrete can't-do-now in the form of being unable to touch his toes or clasp his hands behind his back. The failure here is the most expensive in the batch. In his very first answer the prospect volunteered the deepest motivation anyone offered on any of these seven calls: 'if I want to start a family, or if just want to live longer, you know, to be around for future kids or something, I want to be able to still kind of play with my kids, still pick them up when I'm older.' The rep did return to it - 'You mentioned that your goals have changed now that you're 30... Sounds like having kids. Is this kind of on the radar?' - got 'within the next three to five years', and then closed the thread with 'Okay, got it. It's more of like a future thing then.' From that point the call was about saving time. He then asked for the biggest reason and accepted 'the time element', and his reflect-back converted a longevity-and-family motivation into logistics: 'it's more about the saving the time and having something that you could easily do while traveling.' Nobody asked who else this impacts and nobody drove to family, identity or legacy, on the one call where the prospect had already opened that door himself.

P4.evidence: Past attempts were properly explored - personal trainers, no online coach, and the stretching centre - and what happened with the last one produced a sharp answer: 'I kind of stopped going just because I can't stay consistent in like doing all the stretching. And yeah, their business model is like, they want you to keep coming back. So they never, they don't want you to remember the stretches... And each time you go, it's like over $100 per session.' That is a prospect naming distrust of a provider's incentives, and the rep did later mirror it back well when contrasting the programme's aim of making itself unnecessary. What did not happen was the root-cause work on the real pattern: the travel cycle that wipes out every training block. It was identified factually and never interrogated as a structural problem, and the 'why can't you stick to it on your own' move never ran.

P5.evidence: Not run - the seventh consecutive sales call in this batch with the entire 20-point Consequence Frame absent, and the one where the prospect had already written it himself. At 00:10:34 he volunteered: 'I hear a lot of horror stories about, you people, as they get older, they just, their bodies almost become like petrified, right? It's just like, they can barely move or they like, you know, like guys, like hunch over, right? Like, I want to avoid all that kind of stuff.' That is a two-year question answered before it was asked, attached to a man who wants to pick up children he does not yet have. The response was 'Hmm. Okay' followed by a question about logistics. No 'what does that look like if nothing changes', no 'are you willing to settle for that', no 'why not', no line in the sand.

P6.evidence: No commitment check before presenting. The closest thing was a temperature question after the pitch - 'how do you feel about it?' - which drew a soft 'it seems interesting. I'm definitely down to learn more', and the rep moved to next steps on that. Neither the belief question nor the all-in question was asked. Had the all-in question been put, the trial objection would have surfaced before the price rather than after it, which is the entire reason the script places it where it does.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted and no payment was collected. The onboarding sequence was described in advance - community, app, Trevor connection, onboarding form - but never reached. The call ended with the prospect leaving for another meeting and an open item pending on what Trevor would say about a three-month package.

objection_plays.detail: The clearest fear objection in the batch, stated in the prospect's own words: 'It's a bit of a leap for me in terms of just faith.' The rep eventually produced a real risk reversal - the love-it-or-leave-it guarantee - which is exactly the right instrument, but he produced it at 00:42:14, after the prospect had twice said he would think about it and immediately before he left for another call. None of the scripted moves ran: no 'would it be fair to say you're looking for certainty', no pleasure-versus-pain question, no bridge frame, no plane frame, no burned-before frame, and crucially no 'how will you know if you never actually try', which is the direct answer to a prospect asking for a trial. The material to close this call existed and arrived roughly five minutes too late.

Trigger was 'let me think about it a bit and then I'll get back to you guys.' The isolate ran well and is worth crediting - 'if like six months is too big of a commitment, I guess is that what's coming up for you? Is this like, well, like, I don't even know if I want to work with Trevor 100%' - and the prospect confirmed it exactly. That is the play working. What followed was not the play: instead of 'do you feel what we've gone through can get you there', 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', or the decision-identity move, the rep went to a shorter, cheaper tier framed as needing the founder's sign-off.

No money objection was ever raised - the prospect did not react to $6,000 or $9,000 at all. The rep nonetheless volunteered a payment plan unprompted: 'we can split it up... you don't necessarily have to throw it all on credit card or something like that right away.' Offering to break up a price nobody has objected to invites a concern that did not exist.
No timing objection - the opposite. Asked how quickly he would start, he said 'pretty much ASAP' and 'I'm ready.'
No spousal consult. He is not married and the decision was entirely his own.

A demand for proof of service before purchase, asked three separate ways - a trial, a couple of sessions first, or pay-per-session. This is the same gap that appeared on the Vibhor Mishra call at the start of this batch, where the prospect asked repeatedly for a sample plan, and it has no scripted play and no product answer. Here it is sharper because the prospect explicitly said it need not be free: 'It doesn't have to be a free trial.' There is a real commercial answer available - a paid first month under the existing guarantee - and it exists as an ad-hoc mention rather than as a defined offer, which is why it arrived at the end of the call instead of the middle.

notes: The one call in the batch that could have closed on the strength of what the prospect volunteered, and it was lost in the first two minutes rather than the last five. He handed over a family-and-longevity motivation and a ready-made consequence frame about men becoming petrified with age, and both were converted into a conversation about travel logistics. Coach three things: never write off a stated why because it is three to five years out, run the guarantee as the answer to a trial request the moment it is asked, and do not invent a founder-approval frame for a tier already being sold as standard.
